outcome: Woodall's conjecture itself (general, unweighted digraphs) remains fully open with no resolution, no disproof, and no genuinely new bound first announced inside the window; the one true bound on the unweighted conjecture (Cornuéjols, Liu, Ravi, 'Approximately Packing Dijoins via Nowhere-Zero Flows') was first posted to arXiv on 2023-11-07, before the frozen revision, and only its IPCO 2024 conference presentation (2024-07-03/05) and later journal publication (Combinatorica, 2025) fall inside the window; everything else found in the window (chordal-digraph result, p-adic relaxation, dual-conjecture partial-3-trees result) settles a related-but-different conjecture rather than a case of Woodall's own statement.
summary: Woodall's conjecture (1976) as stated in the bullet — for a general digraph, minimum dicut size equals maximum number of disjoint dijoins — is still open. Nothing in the window resolves it, disproves it, or produces a genuinely new bound whose first written argument falls inside the window. Four pieces of related work surfaced: (1) Cornuéjols, Liu, Ravi, 'Approximately Packing Dijoins via Nowhere-Zero Flows' (arXiv:2311.04337) is the one paper that actually bounds the unweighted Woodall conjecture directly, proving a digraph with minimum dicut size τ contains ⌊τ/k⌋ disjoint dijoins whenever the underlying graph admits a nowhere-zero k-flow (giving ⌊τ/6⌋ unconditionally via Seymour 1981). Its v1 was posted 2023-11-07, before the frozen revision, so under §6.3 the event is dated to that preprint and the status is open_stale; its IPCO 2024 Best Paper presentation (Wrocław, 2024-07-03 to 07-05) and its 2025 Combinatorica journal publication (and arXiv v2, 2025-05-22) are the only window-internal traces of it, representing further vetting/digestion of an already-existing result rather than a new one. (2) Cornuéjols, Liu, Ravi, 'A Min-Max Relation on Dicuts and Dijoins in Weighted Chordal Digraphs' (arXiv:2501.10918, Jan 2025) resolves the weighted Edmonds-Giles conjecture (a distinct, related conjecture already known to be false in general) for chordal digraphs; per its own abstract 'the unweighted version conjectured by Woodall remains open' — this is a related problem, not a case of Woodall's own statement, so it does not count under §3.1. (3) Abdi, Cornuéjols, Liu, Silina, 'Strongly connected orientations and integer lattices' (arXiv:2410.13665, Oct 2024, in window) proves a p-adic (fractional/relaxed) packing relaxation of Woodall's conjecture — this changes what is being packed (p-adic rather than integer dijoins), making it a variant rather than a restriction, so it also does not count as a case. (4) Gutiérrez, 'Towards a Dual Version of Woodall's Conjecture for Partial 3-Trees' (arXiv:2408.05703, Aug 2024) explicitly addresses a dual conjecture (shortest dicycle vs. disjoint feedback arc sets in planar digraphs), which is a different, though related, statement. A separate 'Seymour and Woodall's conjecture' (2001, on chromatic number and complete bipartite minors) is an unrelated conjecture sharing Woodall's name and was excluded. No AI system was mentioned in any of the primary sources checked; all listed results are conventional human-authored combinatorial proofs. Net: no in-window event changes what a careful person would write in this bullet; the closest thing to real progress on the unweighted conjecture predates the window and only received further vetting (conference award, journal publication) inside it.
competing_reading: One could argue the IPCO 2024 Best Paper presentation (July 2024) or the Combinatorica 2025 journal publication of arXiv:2311.04337 should itself be treated as the 'event' under the conference/journal-postdate exception discussed in §6.3 ('announced at a conference before the frozen date but written up after') — but here the arXiv preprint already existed before the frozen date, so this exception (meant for results only written up after being announced) does not apply, and the paper is more naturally treated as fully predating the window, hence open_stale rather than progress. If one instead credits the paper's continued life (award, journal version) as evidence the community's understanding of the bound genuinely firmed up within the window, `progress` with the later date could be argued instead.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the field would consider a paper 'new' for dating purposes when its first arXiv posting predates the window but its peer-reviewed publication and major award fall inside it; and whether a future paper actually restricts Woodall's own unweighted statement (e.g., to chordal digraphs, without changing weighted/unweighted or integer/p-adic character) rather than a neighboring conjecture.
